steps.title: Sign in to GitHub
steps.notes: The new-app URL redirects straight to github.com/login with return_to set. No developer program, waitlist or approval in front of the form. Options: password, Google, Apple, passkey.

steps.title: Open Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App
steps.quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Shortcut: after signing in, https://github.com/settings/applications/new opens the form directly. If no app exists yet the button reads 'Register a new application'.

steps.title: Fill in Application name, Homepage URL and (optional) description
steps.notes: Agent can prepare the values; a human types them into the signed-in form. Docs warn to use only information you consider public.

steps.title: Set Authorization callback URL to Composio's callback
steps.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Value to paste: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (per Composio docs; copy the exact value shown in your Composio auth config, since some toolkits still show the legacy v1 URL).

steps.title: Decide on 'Expire user access tokens' (on by default)
steps.quote: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Leave it on if your token handling supports refresh (Composio refreshes tokens for you).

steps.title: Click Register application
steps.notes: No review or approval follows. The app works immediately.

steps.title: Generate a client secret and paste client ID + secret into a Composio auth config
steps.notes: Not shown on the captured docs page and not visible without signing in. From our earlier research only; check on first sign-in.

blocked_at.what_it_asks_for: A GitHub account (username or email + password, or Google/Apple/passkey sign-in).

observations: Console wall reached in one redirect, with no bot check or cookie banner.
The docs page is static and easy to capture; three of three quotes were verified on the live page.
Screenshots show the docs, not the real form. The real form needs a signed-in human.
